newsitem.title: USA: USDA buys 5.15 mln lbs frozen beef for programs.
newsitem.headline: USDA buys 5.15 mln lbs frozen beef for programs.

text.p: The Agricultural Marketing Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it bought about five million lbs of frozen beef for distribution in the National School Lunch Program and other Federal programs.

Since May 1, when USDA announced an accelerated beef buying initiative to aid the cattle industry, the government has bought about 55 million pounds of beef products at a cost of about $51 million, the AMS said.
The latest award under Announcement LS-48, Invitation 012, will be shipped between October 5 and 18, 1996.
Details of this week's purchase are as follows:
Total purchases since the program was announced:

Winning bidders for the fine frozen ground beef were Emmpak Foods Inc (Milwaukee WI) 396,000 lbs, Fresno Meat Co (Fresno CA) 594,000 lbs, Northern States Beef (Omaha NE) 1,346,400 lbs, Supreme Beef Processors (Dallas TX) 1,108,800 lbs, Surlean Meat Co (San Antonio TX) 475,200 lbs, and Taylor Packing Co (Wyalusing PA) 39,600 lbs.
Winning bidder for frozen beef patties with VPP was Service Packing Co (Joplin MO) 554,400 lbs.
Winning bidder for frozen beef patties 100 pct beef was Service Packing Co (Joplin MO) 158,400 lbs.
Winning bidders for the frozen beef patties (lean) were Aksarben Foods Inc (Omaha NE) 39,600 lbs and Supreme Beef Processors (Dallas TX) 158,400 lbs.
